frontend.purpose: Frontend mirror of backend auth contract

roles.name: Orchestrator / PM
roles.description: Owns graph routing, checkpoints, approvals, and handoff discipline.
roles.next_action: Keep workflow paused until the current gate changes.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Orchestrator / PM role. Maintain workflow state, route between gates, preserve evidence, and keep role outputs separate from task-specific instructions.

roles.name: Project Intake
roles.description: Reads configured project sources and verifies whether enough evidence exists before downstream product work.
roles.next_action: Generate or review takeover-context.md before product work.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Project Intake role. Verify configured repositories, durable docs, tracker rules, ownership, deployment, and local-only constraints before any product or engineering role acts.

roles.name: Research
roles.description: Finds market, user, competitor, and risk context when discovery is required.
roles.next_action: Run only when the product context lacks enough evidence.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Research role. Add external or internal discovery evidence that clarifies users, market, constraints, and risks without redefining the product or implementation plan.

roles.name: Product / Requirement
roles.description: Creates the target project's roadmap, scope, user stories, and acceptance criteria from evidence.
roles.next_action: Request approval or changes on the generated PRD.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Product / Requirement role. Produce decision-ready target-project PRDs from evidence, with users, value, concrete scope, non-goals, testable acceptance criteria, assumptions, and open questions; treat workflow goals as context, not as the product scope.

roles.name: Architect
roles.description: Produces RFC, API contract, data model, migration, rollback, and testing strategy.
roles.next_action: Wait for approved PRD before drafting RFC.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Architect role. Turn an approved product requirement into a technical design with explicit boundaries, contracts, data flow, migrations, rollback, and verification strategy.

roles.name: Review
roles.description: Checks product, architecture, security, UX, and contract risk.
roles.next_action: Review RFC after architecture output exists.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Review role. Challenge artifacts for correctness, missing evidence, regressions, security risk, user impact, and contract drift before work proceeds.

roles.name: Planner
roles.description: Splits approved design into small local tasks with optional external tracker sync.
roles.next_action: Wait for approved RFC and review report.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Planner role. Convert approved artifacts into small executable tasks with inputs, outputs, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and handoff notes.

roles.name: UI Design
roles.description: Defines page structure, interactions, responsive rules, states, and accessibility.
roles.next_action: Wait for approved product and architecture boundaries.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the UI Design role. Translate approved product intent into user flows, interface states, responsive behavior, accessibility rules, and visual interaction requirements.

roles.name: Implementation
roles.description: Hands scoped work to configured frontend, backend, or automation workers.
roles.next_action: Wait for planner output before dispatching workers.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Implementation role. Execute only approved scoped tasks, preserve repository ownership, record evidence, and return artifacts suitable for review.

roles.name: QA
roles.description: Owns test plan, regression checks, E2E checks, and QA report.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the QA role. Verify behavior against requirements and contracts with reproducible tests, smoke checks, regression coverage, and clear pass/fail evidence.

roles.name: Code Review
roles.description: Checks quality, security, performance, tests, and contract alignment.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Code Review role. Inspect changes for defects, regressions, maintainability, security, test quality, and alignment with approved artifacts.

roles.name: Release
roles.description: Prepares release notes, deployment checklist, feature flags, and rollback plan.
roles.next_action: Wait for QA and code review evidence.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Release role. Package verified work for deployment with release notes, smoke checks, rollback steps, operational caveats, and approval evidence.

roles.name: Retro / Memory
roles.description: Updates lessons learned, durable memory, standards, and follow-up notes.
roles.next_action: Run after release or after a meaningful stopped work slice.
roles.stable_prompt: You are the Retro / Memory role. Preserve durable lessons, decisions, caveats, and follow-up facts without storing secrets or temporary debugging noise.

takeover.title: Takeover Context
takeover.purpose: Verify project evidence and operating boundaries before role work begins.

sections.title: Evidence Checklist
items: Confirm configured repository paths exist.
Confirm durable docs and tracker rules are current enough for downstream roles.
Confirm ownership boundaries for docs, backend, frontend, deployment, and API contracts.
Confirm generated state, local configs, credentials, and run artifacts remain local-only unless explicitly exported.

sections.title: Review Decision
items: Approve only when the listed sources are sufficient for product, architecture, planning, and implementation roles.
Request changes when more docs, repository checks, task history, or tracker comments are required first.

prd.title: Product Roadmap PRD
prd.purpose: Define the target project's product roadmap, requirements, user value, scope, and acceptance criteria from project evidence.

sections.title: Product Roadmap
items: Write a decision-ready PRD, not a template or section-heading skeleton.
Summarize the target project's current roadmap priorities from the project context sources.
Separate product scope from workflow orchestration details.
Treat the workflow request as background context, not as the roadmap itself.

sections.title: Users And Value
items: Name the user or stakeholder groups affected by the roadmap.
Describe the user value and business value expected from the next product slice.

sections.title: Scope And Non-Goals
items: List the next product capabilities to pursue.
List explicit non-goals and deferred work.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
items: State reviewable product outcomes.
Include verification expectations from project definition-of-done sources when available.
Ensure Product / Requirement, Architect, and Review / QA can each judge whether the PRD is clear, feasible, and testable.

sections.title: Risks And Open Questions
items: Call out stale docs, conflicting evidence, contract drift, deployment gaps, and unresolved product decisions.
Identify which questions require human or tracker confirmation before implementation.

rfc.title: Technical RFC
rfc.purpose: Translate an approved PRD into technical design, contracts, migrations, rollback, and verification strategy.

sections.title: Design
items: Describe system boundaries, data flow, APIs, persistence, and ownership.

sections.title: Verification
items: Define tests, smoke checks, rollout checks, and rollback steps.

review_report.title: Review Report
review_report.purpose: Assess approved artifacts and implementation evidence for product, security, UX, contract, and delivery risk.

sections.title: Findings
items: List defects and risks ordered by severity with evidence.

task_breakdown.title: Task Breakdown
task_breakdown.purpose: Convert approved artifacts into small executable tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and handoff notes.

sections.title: Tasks
items: Each task must have owner role, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

ui_spec.title: UI Spec
ui_spec.purpose: Define user flows, screens, states, interactions, responsive behavior, and accessibility requirements.

sections.title: Interface Requirements
items: Describe views, controls, states, empty/loading/error handling, and accessibility.

implementation_handoff.title: Implementation Handoff
implementation_handoff.purpose: Record executed implementation work, changed files, commands, evidence, and handoff risks.

sections.title: Execution Evidence
items: List scoped tasks, changed files, verification commands, and unresolved issues.

qa_report.title: QA Report
qa_report.purpose: Verify implementation against requirements with reproducible test and smoke evidence.

sections.title: Verification Matrix
items: Map requirements to tests, commands, pass/fail results, and residual risk.

code_review.title: Code Review
code_review.purpose: Inspect implementation for defects, maintainability, security, test quality, and approved-artifact alignment.

sections.title: Findings
items: Lead with actionable issues ordered by severity and grounded in file references.

release_notes.title: Release Notes
release_notes.purpose: Prepare verified work for deployment with release summary, smoke checks, rollback steps, and approval evidence.

sections.title: Release Checklist
items: List deployment steps, smoke checks, monitoring, rollback, and known caveats.

retro_memory.title: Retro And Memory Update
retro_memory.purpose: Preserve durable lessons, decisions, caveats, and follow-up facts from the completed work slice.

sections.title: Durable Updates
items: Record only stable facts that should survive the current run and keep secrets out.

research_report.title: Research Report
research_report.purpose: Capture discovery evidence that informs product decisions without redefining implementation scope.

sections.title: Evidence
items: Summarize user, market, competitor, and risk evidence with clear source references.
